```markdown
# User Data Export: Implementation Tasks

Plan: build an API endpoint that exports all of a user's data. Format: whatever is easiest. Should be fast. Ship next week.

## 1. Decisions to pin down (quick, ~30 min total)
- [ ] Choose the format. Default to JSON, since it is the easiest and handles nested data.
- [ ] Define "all of a user's data" by listing every table/service that holds user-owned data.
- [ ] Set a concrete "fast" target (e.g. p95 latency or max export size) so it can be tested.
- [ ] Decide sync vs. async delivery. Default to sync streaming if the target is met, with async as a fallback for large accounts.

## 2. Data inventory
- [ ] List all data stores and tables with user-linked records.
- [ ] Mark fields to exclude (password hashes, tokens, internal flags, other users' data).
- [ ] Note any data in third-party systems that is out of scope for v1.

## 3. Backend implementation
- [ ] Add the endpoint (e.g. `GET /api/users/me/export`).
- [ ] Add an authentication check so users can export only their own data.
- [ ] Add per-source collectors that each return one user's records.
- [ ] Add a serializer that assembles the collector output into the chosen format.
- [ ] Stream the response or paginate queries to avoid loading everything into memory.
- [ ] Add rate limiting, since the endpoint is expensive.
- [ ] Return appropriate errors (401/403/429/500) with a consistent shape.

## 4. Performance
- [ ] Check queries for missing indexes on user_id foreign keys.
- [ ] Avoid N+1 queries in the collectors.
- [ ] Load test with a large synthetic account against the target from section 1.

## 5. Security and privacy
- [ ] Verify that no other user's data or secrets appear in the output.
- [ ] Add audit logging of export requests (user, time, size).
- [ ] Set response headers (`Content-Disposition`, `Cache-Control: no-store`).

## 6. Testing
- [ ] Unit tests for each collector and the serializer.
- [ ] Integration test: the export contains the expected data for a seeded user.
- [ ] Authorization tests: unauthenticated and cross-user access are rejected.
- [ ] Edge cases: empty account, very large account, special characters in data.

## 7. Release
- [ ] Document the endpoint (request, response schema, limits).
- [ ] Put it behind a feature flag and roll out gradually.
- [ ] Add monitoring/alerts for latency and error rate.
- [ ] Final QA and sign-off, then ship next week.

## Suggested order
1 → 2 → 3 (in parallel with 6) → 4 → 5 → 7
```

Section 1 isn't meant to reopen the plan. Those few items are what the engineers will need answered on day one: format, scope, and a testable "fast" target.
